topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A Nebraska broker refuses to show a rental property to a prospective tenant because of the tenant's national origin. Under the Nebraska Real Estate License Act, this conduct is:
choice_a: An unfair trade practice subjecting the broker to discipline
choice_b: Permitted, because rental decisions are solely the property owner's prerogative
choice_c: Only actionable under federal law, not Nebraska statute
choice_d: Permitted as long as the broker does not advertise the refusal
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(1) makes it an unfair trade practice for a licensee to refuse to show, sell, or rent property to any person because of religion, race, color, national origin, ethnic group, sex, familial status, disability, or military or veteran status. The Real Estate Commission may investigate and discipline a licensee for this conduct independent of any federal fair housing claim.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker represents both the buyer and the seller in a transaction but does not tell either party that the other is also a client. Which unfair trade practice has the broker committed?
choice_a: Filing a cloud on title
choice_b: Acting for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge of all parties for whom the broker acts
choice_c: Acting in the dual capacity of agent and undisclosed principal
choice_d: Commingling trust funds
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(23) prohibits a licensee from acting for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge of all parties for whom he or she acts. This is distinct from subsection (9), which addresses a broker acting as an undisclosed principal (i.e., secretly buying or selling for the broker's own account).

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker purchases a property listed with her own brokerage through a straw buyer without disclosing to the seller that she is the true purchaser. This is an unfair trade practice known as:
choice_a: A right-to-list home sale agreement violation
choice_b: Blockbusting
choice_c: Acting in the dual capacity of agent and undisclosed principal
choice_d: Commingling
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(9) specifically prohibits a licensee from acting in the dual capacity of agent and undisclosed principal in any transaction. Buying through a straw party while acting as the listing agent, without disclosure, falls squarely within this provision.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A salesperson tells a buyer, 'Don't worry about the resale value — I personally guarantee you'll make at least $20,000 in profit if you sell in five years.' This statement violates which provision of the License Act?
choice_a: The prohibition on undisclosed dual agency
choice_b: The recordkeeping requirement for closing statements
choice_c: The prohibition on commingling
choice_d: The prohibition on guaranteeing or authorizing any person to guarantee future profits from the resale of real property
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(10) makes it an unfair trade practice to guarantee or authorize any person to guarantee future profits which may result from the resale of real property. Speculative profit guarantees expose buyers to risk the licensee cannot control.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee talks a seller into breaking an existing purchase agreement with one buyer so the seller can sign a new contract with a different buyer the licensee represents. This is:
choice_a: A prohibited act — inducing a party to a contract of sale to break it in order to substitute a new contract with another principal
choice_b: Permitted because the seller, not the licensee, made the final decision
choice_c: Permitted if the original buyer has not yet closed
choice_d: Only a civil matter between the two buyers, outside the Commission's jurisdiction
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(13) prohibits inducing any party to a contract of sale or lease to break such contract for the purpose of substituting a new contract with another principal. The Commission has jurisdiction over this conduct as an unfair trade practice regardless of whether the seller ultimately consented.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Broker A knows that a homeowner has a written exclusive-right-to-sell listing with Broker B. Broker A contacts the homeowner directly and negotiates a new listing to replace the one with Broker B. Broker A has violated the License Act by:
choice_a: Commingling client funds
choice_b: Negotiating directly with an owner known to have an outstanding exclusive listing contract with another broker for the purpose of substituting a new listing contract
choice_c: Failing to maintain a trust account
choice_d: Violating the branch office licensing requirement
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(14) prohibits negotiating a sale, exchange, listing, or lease directly with an owner known to have a written outstanding exclusive listing with another broker, or negotiating with the owner to withdraw from or break that listing to substitute a new one.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A property is exclusively listed with Broker X. Broker Y, without being asked by the owner, approaches the owner to discuss the terms under which Broker Y would accept the listing once Broker X's agreement expires. This is:
choice_a: Not addressed by the Nebraska Real Estate License Act
choice_b: Permitted at any time before the listing expires
choice_c: A prohibited act unless the owner initiated the discussion
choice_d: Permitted only if Broker Y first notifies Broker X in writing
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(15) prohibits discussing or soliciting discussion, with an owner whose property is exclusively listed with another broker, of the terms on which the broker would accept a future listing upon expiration of the current one — unless the owner initiates the discussion.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: The Nebraska Real Estate License Act makes it an unfair trade practice for a licensee to violate which other set of Nebraska statutes governing housing discrimination?
choice_a: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1416
choice_c: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(16) makes it an unfair trade practice to violate any provision of sections 76-2401 to 76-2430, which comprise Nebraska's fair housing statutes. A licensee who violates fair housing law is therefore also subject to discipline under the License Act itself.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A brokerage runs a promotion offering a free lot to anyone who attends a sales presentation and enters a drawing, in order to drum up interest in a subdivision. Under Nebraska law, this practice is:
choice_a: An unfair trade practice — soliciting, selling, or offering real estate for sale by offering free lots or conducting lotteries to influence a purchaser
choice_b: Regulated only by federal sweepstakes law, not the License Act
choice_c: Permitted advertising as long as the odds of winning are disclosed
choice_d: Permitted because it does not involve a misrepresentation
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(17) prohibits soliciting, selling, or offering real estate for sale by offering free lots or conducting lotteries for the purpose of influencing a purchaser or prospective purchaser.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A listing agent tells a buyer that a home's roof was replaced two years ago when the agent knows it was never replaced. This is best classified under the License Act as:
choice_a: Undisclosed dual agency
choice_b: A substantial misrepresentation
choice_c: Blockbusting
choice_d: A recordkeeping violation
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(22) makes it an unfair trade practice to make any substantial misrepresentation. A knowingly false statement about a material fact such as a roof replacement fits this provision directly.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A Nebraska salesperson is convicted of felony theft unrelated to real estate practice. Under the License Act, this conviction:
choice_a: Only matters if the licensee is also disbarred from another profession
choice_b: Cannot be considered by the Commission because it did not occur in the course of licensed activity
choice_c: Is grounds for discipline, including a felony conviction or a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to a felony charge
choice_d: Automatically revokes the license without any hearing rights
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(28) lists conviction of a felony, or entering a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to a felony charge, by a broker or salesperson as an unfair trade practice subject to discipline, regardless of whether the felony arose from licensed real estate activity. The licensee still retains hearing rights under §81-885.25.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker repeatedly makes careless errors in transaction paperwork and demonstrates a pattern of poor judgment that does not fit neatly into any other specifically listed unfair trade practice. The Commission may still discipline the broker under which catch-all provision?
choice_a: Filing a cloud on title
choice_b: Blockbusting
choice_c: Failing to maintain a branch office license
choice_d: Demonstrating negligence, incompetency, or unworthiness to act as a broker, associate broker, or salesperson
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(29) allows discipline for demonstrating negligence, incompetency, or unworthiness to act as a broker, associate broker, or salesperson, whether of the same or a different character than otherwise specified in the section — a broad catch-all beyond the other enumerated acts.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee tells a homeowner that Hispanic families are moving into the neighborhood and that property values are likely to decline as a result, urging the homeowner to sell quickly. This conduct is:
choice_a: Blockbusting, an unfair trade practice under the License Act
choice_b: A pricing disclosure violation only
choice_c: Permitted opinion testimony protected as free speech
choice_d: Only a violation if the homeowner actually sells the property
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(30) prohibits inducing or attempting to induce a person to transfer an interest in real property by representing that a change in the neighborhood's racial, ethnic, or other protected composition has occurred or will occur, or that such a change will lower property values — commonly known as blockbusting. The prohibition applies regardless of whether a sale actually results.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A brokerage offers sellers a 'right-to-list home sale agreement' under which the seller agrees the brokerage will have the right to list the home whenever it is eventually sold, in exchange for a discounted upfront service. Under the 2023 amendments to the Nebraska Real Estate License Act, offering or entering into this type of agreement is:
choice_a: Permitted without restriction
choice_b: Expressly designated an unfair trade practice
choice_c: Regulated only under federal RESPA rules
choice_d: Expressly required for all cash-offer programs
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(37) makes offering or entering into a right-to-list home sale agreement an unfair trade practice, reflecting the Legislature's concern with agreements that lock property owners into future listing obligations, often tied to services like cash-offer or bridge-financing programs.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker accepts a rebate from a home warranty company for referring clients, without telling the clients about the payment. This is an unfair trade practice because it constitutes:
choice_a: Blockbusting
choice_c: Accepting, giving, or charging a form of undisclosed compensation, consideration, rebate, or direct profit on expenditures made for a principal
choice_b: A violation of the branch office statute
choice_d: A recordkeeping violation only
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(6) prohibits accepting, giving, or charging any form of undisclosed compensation, consideration, rebate, or direct profit on expenditures made for a principal. Referral payments tied to client-related expenditures must be disclosed to the principal.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: An online listing for a Nebraska home states it has a finished basement and a three-car garage, features the property does not have, in order to generate more showings. This advertisement violates:
choice_a: The 72-hour trust deposit rule
choice_b: The subdivider compliance requirement
choice_c: The branch office licensing statute
choice_d: The prohibition on intentionally using advertising which is misleading or inaccurate in any material particular
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(2) makes it an unfair trade practice to intentionally use advertising that is misleading or inaccurate in any material particular. Listing false features such as a finished basement or extra garage bays that do not exist is a material misrepresentation in advertising.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A team within a Nebraska brokerage advertises itself as 'Summit Realty Group' on yard signs and social media without any reference to the name of the brokerage under which its designated broker actually does business. This most directly violates the requirement that:
choice_a: Advertising must prominently display the name under which the designated broker does business as filed with the Commission
choice_b: All advertising must be pre-approved by the Commission before publication
choice_c: All advertising must include the seller's asking price
choice_d: Teams may not use any name other than the individual agents' legal names
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(33) prohibits advertising that does not prominently display the name under which the designated broker does business as filed with the Commission. A team name alone, without the brokerage's filed business name, fails this requirement.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A team calls itself 'Platinum Home Advisors' in its marketing in a way that implies it is a separate, independent brokerage from the firm that actually holds the team members' licenses. This is a violation because:
choice_a: The name must be registered as a trademark before use
choice_b: Team advertising or a team name may not suggest that the team is an independent real estate brokerage
choice_c: Only licensed brokers, not teams, may advertise at all
choice_d: Teams are never permitted to use a distinct name
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(34) prohibits utilizing team advertising or a team name suggesting that the team is an independent real estate brokerage, since a team operates under, and is supervised by, a single designated broker.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 2, require that a broker's filed business name appear in advertising in a manner that is:
choice_a: In a font size no smaller than the licensee's personal name
choice_b: Included only in print advertising, not digital advertising
choice_c: Conspicuous, discernible, and easily identifiable by the public
choice_d: Printed only in the brokerage's registered trademark colors
explanation: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 2, implement the statutory advertising name-display requirement of §81-885.24(33) by requiring that the broker's name, as filed with the Commission, be conspicuous, discernible, and easily identifiable by the public in advertising, including team and affiliate advertising.
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 2

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker places a 'For Sale' sign in the yard of a property before the owner has signed anything authorizing it, believing the owner will list with the brokerage soon. This is a violation because a licensee may not:
choice_a: Advertise a property using a photograph without a licensed photographer
choice_b: Place any sign without first obtaining a branch office license
choice_c: Use any sign larger than the local zoning code allows
choice_d: Place a sign on any property offering it for sale or rent without the written consent of the owner or the owner's authorized agent
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(11) prohibits placing a sign on any property offering it for sale or rent without the written consent of the owner or the owner's authorized agent. Anticipating consent is not sufficient; written authorization must exist before the sign goes up.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A salesperson lists and advertises a rental unit for $1,400 per month when the actual owner-authorized rent is $1,600, hoping to generate more calls and then negotiate the price up. This violates the prohibition on:
choice_a: Offering real estate for sale or lease without the knowledge and consent of the owner or on terms other than those authorized
choice_b: Filing a cloud on title
choice_c: Accepting compensation from a non-employing broker
choice_d: Failing to maintain a trust account
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(12) prohibits offering real estate for sale or lease without the knowledge and consent of the owner or the owner's authorized agent, or on terms other than those authorized. Advertising a different rental price than the owner authorized falls within this prohibition.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A brokerage's website lists dozens of properties as 'available' weeks after they have sold, without updating the site, because updating listings is not a priority for the office manager. Under the License Act's advertising standard, stale listings presented as currently available are most likely to be treated as:
choice_a: A permissible marketing practice since the properties were genuinely for sale at some point
choice_b: Advertising that is misleading or inaccurate in a material particular
choice_c: Acceptable as long as a disclaimer appears somewhere on the website
choice_d: A recordkeeping violation only, with no advertising implications
explanation: Representing sold or unavailable properties as currently available materially misleads consumers about what is actually on the market, which falls within the §81-885.24(2) prohibition on intentionally misleading or materially inaccurate advertising when the licensee knows or should know the listings are stale.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: An associate broker advertises a listing using only her personal nickname and cell phone number, with no reference anywhere in the ad to the brokerage's name filed with the Commission. This advertisement is:
choice_a: Acceptable because associate brokers may advertise independently of their employing broker
choice_b: Regulated only if the ad is placed in print media
choice_c: Deficient because advertising must prominently display the name under which the designated broker does business as filed with the Commission
choice_d: Acceptable as long as the associate broker's license number appears somewhere
explanation: The advertising-name requirement of Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(33) applies to advertising by any licensee, including an associate broker, and requires the designated broker's filed business name to be prominently displayed, not merely the individual licensee's personal branding.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A team's Facebook page displays the team's own logo prominently at the top of every post, with the designated broker's filed business name appearing only once, in very small gray text at the bottom of the 'About' section. This arrangement most likely fails NREC's advertising rule because the broker's name is not:
choice_a: Displayed in the same font as the team logo
choice_b: Preceded by the word 'licensed'
choice_c: Registered as a federal trademark
choice_d: Conspicuous, discernible, and easily identifiable by the public
explanation: Title 299, Chapter 2 requires the broker's filed name to be conspicuous, discernible, and easily identifiable by the public in team and affiliate advertising — a standard that burying the name in small, low-visibility text fails to meet, even if the name technically appears somewhere on the page.
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 2; Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(33)

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker receives an earnest money check from a buyer along with a fully executed, written offer that the seller accepts on a Monday morning. Absent a written agreement between the parties to the contrary, Nebraska trust account rules generally require the broker to deposit the earnest money:
choice_a: Within 72 hours, or by the end of the next banking day after written acceptance of the offer, whichever applies
choice_b: At any time before the transaction is consummated
choice_c: Only after the buyer's loan is fully underwritten
choice_d: Within 30 calendar days of closing
explanation: The NREC Trust Account Manual's '72-hour rule' requires a broker to deposit earnest money into the trust account within 72 hours, or by the end of the next banking day after written acceptance of the offer, whichever applies, unless all parties agree otherwise in writing.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: All parties to a purchase agreement sign a written addendum agreeing that the buyer's earnest money check will not be deposited until loan approval is obtained, which may take longer than 72 hours. Is this permissible under Nebraska trust account rules?
choice_a: No, the 72-hour deposit rule can never be altered under any circumstances
choice_b: Yes, because the 72-hour/next-banking-day deposit rule may be varied if all parties having an interest in the funds agree otherwise in writing
choice_c: No, only the Commission itself can authorize a delayed deposit
choice_d: Yes, but only for commercial transactions, never residential
explanation: Both the trust account statute and the NREC Trust Account Manual recognize that the standard deposit timing may be modified if all parties having an interest in the funds agree otherwise in writing, per Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(5) and the Trust Account Manual's 72-hour rule.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(5); NREC Trust Account Manual

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker deposits client earnest money into the same checking account used to pay the brokerage's rent and utility bills. This is a violation of the prohibition on:
choice_a: Filing a cloud on title
choice_b: Team advertising
choice_c: Commingling the money or other property of principals with the licensee's own
choice_d: Blockbusting
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(4) prohibits commingling the money or other property of principals with the licensee's own. Depositing client trust funds into an operating account used for business expenses is a textbook commingling violation.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker who acts as escrow agent for a for-sale-by-owner transaction, holding the buyer's deposit temporarily, must:
choice_a: Hold the funds in cash in a locked office drawer
choice_b: Return the funds directly to the buyer regardless of the transaction outcome
choice_c: Deposit the funds into the broker's personal savings account for safekeeping
choice_d: Maintain and deposit the funds in a separate trust account unless all parties having an interest in the funds have agreed otherwise in writing
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(5) requires a broker acting in that capacity, or as escrow agent or temporary custodian of others' funds in a real estate transaction, to maintain and deposit all such money in a separate trust account, unless all interested parties have agreed otherwise in writing.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker fails to remit a security deposit refund that is due to a former tenant after deducting proper charges, keeping the money in the trust account indefinitely without explanation. This is most directly a violation of the prohibition on:
choice_a: Failing to account for and remit any money coming into the licensee's possession belonging to others
choice_b: Discussing future listing terms without invitation
choice_c: Placing a sign without consent
choice_d: Violating the branch office statute
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(3) prohibits failing to account for and remit any money coming into a licensee's possession that belongs to others. A broker managing property trust funds must promptly account for and pay out amounts properly owed.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A salesperson receives an earnest money deposit directly from a buyer at a showing. Under the License Act, the salesperson must:
choice_a: Return the funds to the buyer and instruct the buyer to mail them to the seller
choice_b: Place the deposit in the custody of the employing broker as soon after receipt as practicable
choice_c: Hold the funds until closing and then deliver them directly to the title company
choice_d: Deposit the funds into the salesperson's own personal trust account
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(24) prohibits an associate broker or salesperson from failing to place, as soon after receipt as practicable, deposit money or other funds entrusted to them in the custody of their employing broker. Salespersons and associate brokers do not maintain their own separate trust accounts under the Act.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker deducts part of the earnest money as her commission before the sale transaction has closed or otherwise been terminated. This is prohibited because a licensee may not:
choice_a: Ever charge a commission on any transaction involving earnest money
choice_b: Deposit earnest money in a trust account at all
choice_c: Charge or collect, as part or all of his or her compensation, any part of the earnest money or other money paid to him or her in connection with a real estate transaction until the transaction has been consummated or terminated
choice_d: Accept earnest money in the form of a personal check
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(35) prohibits charging or collecting any part of the earnest money or other transaction funds as compensation until the transaction has been consummated or terminated. Commission may only be taken from these funds once the deal is finished, one way or the other.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3, a broker's general trust account recordkeeping and handling obligations include maintaining:
choice_a: A bond in lieu of a trust account for brokers with fewer than five active listings
choice_b: Cash reserves equal to the broker's total annual commission income
choice_c: A single combined account used for both trust funds and office operating expenses, as long as they are tracked on separate spreadsheets
choice_d: A separate, clearly identified trust or escrow account distinct from the broker's personal and business operating funds, together with supporting records for each transaction
explanation: Title 299, Chapter 3 of the NREC Rules and Regulations sets out the general requirements for trust or escrow accounts, requiring that they be kept separate from personal and operating funds and supported by adequate transaction records, consistent with the statutory separate-account mandate in Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(5).
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A buyer and seller disagree about who is entitled to the earnest money after a failed transaction, and the broker holding the funds does not want to release them to either party unilaterally. Under Nebraska rules, how must the broker handle these disputed funds?
choice_a: Follow the disputed funds procedure set out in NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3-007, retaining the funds in trust pending resolution
choice_b: Deposit the disputed funds into the broker's personal account until the dispute is resolved
choice_c: Immediately release the funds to whichever party demands them first
choice_d: Destroy the check and inform both parties the deal is void
explanation: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3-007, governs the handling of disputed trust funds, generally requiring the broker to retain the disputed funds in the trust account and follow the prescribed procedure (such as interpleader or Commission guidance) rather than releasing them unilaterally to either party.
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3-007

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A landlord's Nebraska property manager holds a former tenant's residential security deposit that remains unclaimed 90 days after the tenant moved out, despite reasonable attempts to locate the tenant. Under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, this unclaimed deposit must ultimately be routed to:
choice_a: The landlord's own operating account permanently
choice_b: The State Treasurer's Unclaimed Property Division after 60 days
choice_c: A charity of the property manager's choosing
choice_d: The Nebraska Real Estate Commission's general fund
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1416, part of the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, directs that unclaimed residential security deposits be routed to the State Treasurer's Unclaimed Property Division after 60 days, not retained indefinitely by the landlord or property manager.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker structures a sale so that the buyer's funds are wired directly by a third-party investor to the seller outside of the broker's trust account and outside the closing agent's oversight, bypassing the transaction's normal accounting. This kind of improper third-party handling of transaction funds is the type of conduct addressed by the License Act's requirements that a broker:
choice_a: Maintain a branch office license for every location
choice_b: Complete continuing education by November 30 of the renewal year
choice_c: Account for and safeguard all funds belonging to others coming into the licensee's possession or control in a transaction
choice_d: Advertise using the broker's filed business name
explanation: Improper third-party closings that circumvent a broker's trust accounting obligations undermine the licensee's core duty, under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(3)-(5), to account for, safeguard, and properly deposit funds belonging to others that come into the licensee's possession or control during a transaction.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(3)-(5); NREC Trust Account Manual guidance on third-party closings

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker's trust account bank statement shows a balance lower than the sum of all clients' funds the broker is currently holding, because the broker withdrew money for personal use intending to replace it before anyone noticed. Beyond commingling, this shortage most directly also violates:
choice_a: The advertising name-display requirement
choice_b: The team leader recordkeeping requirement
choice_c: The branch office manager requirement
choice_d: The duty to account for and remit money belonging to others coming into the licensee's possession
explanation: A trust account shortage caused by personal withdrawals violates both the commingling prohibition in §81-885.24(4) and the separate duty in §81-885.24(3) to account for and remit money belonging to others — the broker cannot remit funds that have already been misappropriated.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under the 72-hour trust deposit rule, if a written offer is accepted on a Friday afternoon and the broker's bank is closed over the weekend, when must the earnest money generally be deposited absent a contrary written agreement?
choice_a: By the end of the next banking day, since that measure controls when it falls later than the 72-hour mark over a weekend or holiday
choice_b: Immediately, before the bank closes on the day of acceptance, with no exceptions
choice_c: Whenever the closing agent requests it, with no independent deadline
choice_d: Not until the following Friday, one full week later
explanation: The 72-hour rule is framed as a deposit deadline of 72 hours, or by the end of the next banking day after written acceptance, whichever applies — meaning weekends and bank holidays can extend the practical deadline to the next banking day the broker's depository institution is open.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker's designated bookkeeper reconciles the trust account monthly but has never been trained on distinguishing disputed funds from routine deposits. When a dispute arises over an earnest money deposit, general Title 299, Chapter 3 trust account principles require the broker to ultimately ensure that:
choice_a: Disputed funds are disbursed to whichever party the bookkeeper believes is more credible
choice_b: Trust account records accurately reflect each client's funds and that disputed items are handled under the Chapter 3-007 disputed funds procedure rather than routine disbursement
choice_c: The trust account is closed until the dispute is resolved
choice_d: The bookkeeper alone bears all licensing liability for any error
explanation: The broker, as the license holder responsible for trust account compliance, must ensure accurate recordkeeping under Title 299, Chapter 3, and that disputed items follow the specific disputed-funds procedure in Chapter 3-007 rather than being disbursed as if routine — delegating bookkeeping does not delegate the broker's regulatory responsibility.
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3 and Chapter 3-007

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A property management broker holds tenant security deposits in the same trust account used for sales earnest money, properly tracking each client's funds with individual ledgers. Is a single trust account for both purposes permissible?
choice_a: Yes, but only if the broker obtains a special property management license
choice_b: No, property management funds may never be held in any trust account
choice_c: Yes, provided the account is properly separated from the broker's personal/operating funds and individual client balances are accurately tracked
choice_d: No, sales earnest money and tenant security deposits must always be in two legally distinct accounts under all circumstances
explanation: The core statutory and rule-based requirement is that trust funds be kept separate from the broker's own money and properly accounted for per client, per Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(4)-(5) and Title 299, Chapter 3; the general trust account rules do not categorically forbid holding both types of client funds in one properly maintained trust account with accurate individual accounting.
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3; Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(4)-(5)

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: At closing, a broker representing the seller fails to deliver to the seller a complete, detailed closing statement showing all receipts and disbursements the broker handled. This omission violates:
choice_a: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01
choice_b: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.19
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(21) requires a broker to deliver to the seller, at the time the transaction is consummated, a complete and detailed closing statement showing all receipts and disbursements the broker handled for the seller, and a similar statement to the buyer, and to retain true copies of these statements in the broker's files.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(21), in addition to delivering closing statements to the buyer and seller, a broker must also:
choice_a: Retain true copies of the closing statements in the broker's files
choice_b: Publish the closing statement figures in a local newspaper
choice_c: Send a copy of the closing statement to the Nebraska Real Estate Commission for every transaction
choice_d: File the closing statements with the county register of deeds
explanation: Section 81-885.24(21) requires a broker not only to deliver detailed closing statements to both the seller and the buyer, but also to retain true copies of those statements in the broker's own files, creating an ongoing recordkeeping obligation tied to every consummated transaction.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker prepares a written listing agreement with a seller but leaves the expiration date blank, intending to fill it in later, and never provides the seller a copy of the signed agreement. This omission violates the requirement to:
choice_a: Notify the buyer's agent of the listing terms in writing
choice_b: Include a fixed date of expiration in any written listing agreement and leave a copy of the agreement with the principal
choice_c: Obtain Commission pre-approval of listing agreement language
choice_d: File the listing agreement with the Register of Deeds
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(19) requires every written listing agreement to include a fixed expiration date and requires the licensee to leave a copy of the agreement with the principal (the seller). An open-ended listing with no expiration date, and no copy provided, violates both requirements.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A buyer signs a purchase agreement on June 1, but the broker does not provide the buyer a completed, dated copy of the agreement until June 20, with no explanation for the delay. This is most likely a violation of:
choice_a: The requirement to disclose team membership
choice_b: The requirement to complete continuing education
choice_c: The requirement to deliver within a reasonable time a completed and dated copy of any purchase agreement or offer to the purchaser and to the seller
choice_d: The requirement to maintain a branch office license
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(20) requires a broker to deliver, within a reasonable time, a completed and dated copy of any purchase agreement or offer to buy or sell real estate to both the purchaser and the seller. A three-week unexplained delay is likely to fall outside a 'reasonable time.'

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A designated broker supervises three teams within the brokerage but keeps no master list identifying which licensees belong to which team or who each team's leader is. This failure violates:
choice_a: The felony-conviction disclosure rule
choice_b: The 72-hour trust deposit rule
choice_c: The advertising name-display rule
choice_d: The designated broker's duty to maintain a record of all team leaders and team members working under him or her
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(32) requires a designated broker to maintain a record of all team leaders and team members working under him or her. A brokerage with active teams but no such internal record is in violation.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A team leader adds two new licensees to her team over the course of a year but never updates or provides any current membership list to the designated broker. This is a violation of the team leader's duty to:
choice_a: Provide a current list of all team members to his or her designated broker
choice_b: Personally supervise every transaction handled by team members
choice_c: File a branch office license application for the team
choice_d: Deposit team commissions into a separate trust account
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(31) requires a team leader to provide a current list of all team members to the designated broker. Failing to update the list as membership changes violates this recordkeeping duty, which works together with the designated broker's parallel duty under subsection (32).

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: An unlicensed marketing assistant regularly helps a broker identify potential sellers by handing out flyers at community events. Before the assistant performs this activity, the broker must provide the assistant with:
choice_a: A branch office manager designation
choice_b: A copy of Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.04 or written instructions explaining the licensure exemption applicable to procuring potential clients or customers
choice_c: A full real estate salesperson's license application
choice_d: A copy of the brokerage's trust account bank statements
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(36) requires providing a copy of §81-885.04 or written instructions explaining the licensure exemption to any unlicensed person who assists in procuring a potential client or customer, so the assistant understands the legal boundaries of unlicensed activity.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A buyer's agent verbally tells the buyer the terms of an accepted counteroffer but never provides a completed written copy, believing a verbal recap is sufficient documentation. Under the License Act, this practice is:
choice_a: Only a violation if the transaction later falls through
choice_b: Acceptable because only listing agreements require written copies
choice_c: A violation of the duty to deliver a completed, dated copy of the purchase agreement or offer to the purchaser and seller
choice_d: Acceptable as long as the buyer does not object
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(20) requires delivery of a completed and dated copy of the purchase agreement or offer — a verbal summary does not satisfy this documentation requirement, regardless of whether the buyer objects or the deal later closes.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A brokerage manages several rental properties and keeps ledgers of security deposits, but the ledgers do not identify which portion of the trust account balance belongs to which specific tenant. Under Title 299, Chapter 3 recordkeeping expectations for trust accounts, this practice is problematic because:
choice_a: Security deposits are exempt from all trust account recordkeeping rules
choice_b: Only sales transactions, not rentals, require any ledger at all
choice_c: Ledgers are optional as long as the bank statement balance is accurate
choice_d: Trust account records must allow each client's or tenant's funds to be individually identified and reconciled, not merely tracked in the aggregate
explanation: General trust account recordkeeping principles under Title 299, Chapter 3 require that records permit each client's funds to be individually identified and reconciled against the account balance, not just tracked in an undifferentiated pool, so that no client's funds are inadvertently used to cover a shortage in another's.
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker's employing salesperson closes a transaction and turns in a purchase agreement copy for the file, but the broker never confirms that the buyer and seller each also received their own dated copies. If neither party ever received a copy, the responsibility for the resulting recordkeeping and delivery violation under §81-885.24(20) rests with:
choice_a: The licensee(s) who failed to ensure delivery, and potentially the supervising designated broker, since the Act imposes the delivery duty on brokers handling the transaction
choice_b: Only the title company handling the closing
choice_c: The buyer and seller, for not requesting copies themselves
choice_d: No one, since the deal already closed
explanation: The delivery duty in §81-885.24(20) falls on the broker (and by extension the salespersons acting on the broker's behalf) handling the transaction; a designated broker's general supervisory responsibility means both the individual licensee and the broker can face scrutiny when required documentation is never delivered.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under the introductory paragraph of Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24, the Nebraska Real Estate Commission may investigate a licensee's conduct:
choice_a: Only if the Nebraska Attorney General first authorizes the investigation
choice_b: Upon its own motion, and must investigate upon the sworn written complaint of any person
choice_c: Only after a criminal conviction has already occurred
choice_d: Only upon its own motion, never in response to a complaint
explanation: The introductory language of §81-885.24 provides that the Commission may, upon its own motion, and shall, upon the sworn complaint in writing of any person, investigate the actions of a broker, associate broker, salesperson, or subdivider for unfair trade practices.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: If a license was procured through false or fraudulent representation, the Nebraska Real Estate Commission may respond by:
choice_a: Only revoking the license, with no other options available
choice_b: Taking no action unless a criminal court has already ruled on the fraud
choice_c: Censuring the licensee, revoking or suspending the license, entering a consent order, or imposing a civil fine, alone or in combination
choice_d: Referring the matter exclusively to federal authorities
explanation: Section 81-885.24 authorizes the Commission to censure the licensee, revoke or suspend the license or certificate, enter into consent orders, and, alone or in combination with such actions, impose a civil fine under §81-885.10, whenever a license was obtained by false or fraudulent representation or the licensee is found guilty of an unfair trade practice.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker pays an unlicensed friend a flat fee for referring a buyer who later purchases a home, and the friend is not a nonresident licensed elsewhere nor a qualifying foreign-resident referrer. This payment violates:
choice_a: The prohibition on commingling
choice_b: The subdivider compliance requirement
choice_c: The branch office manager requirement
choice_d: The prohibition on providing compensation to a person for performing broker or salesperson services without a Nebraska license, outside the narrow referral-fee exceptions
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(18) prohibits compensating an unlicensed person for performing broker/salesperson services, except for a referral fee paid to a nonresident licensed in their own jurisdiction or a qualifying foreign-resident broker. A friend with no license and no qualifying status does not fall within either exception.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A disgruntled former listing broker records a document purporting to create a lien based on an expired listing contract, with no valid remaining claim, purely to complicate the seller's ability to sell to a new agent. This act is prohibited as:
choice_a: Filing a listing contract or document purporting to create a lien for the purpose of casting a cloud on title when no valid claim exists
choice_b: A permissible method of enforcing a commission dispute
choice_c: A recordkeeping violation only
choice_d: An advertising violation
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(25) prohibits filing a listing contract or any document purporting to create a lien based on it, for the purpose of clouding title to real estate, when no valid claim under the listing contract actually exists.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: The Nebraska Real Estate Commission adopts a new rule addressing electronic signature practices in real estate transactions. A licensee who knowingly disregards this properly adopted rule has:
choice_a: Only violated a suggestion, not an enforceable requirement
choice_b: Committed an unfair trade practice by violating a rule or regulation adopted by the commission
choice_c: Committed a violation only if a client is financially harmed
choice_d: Not committed any violation, since only statutes (not Commission rules) can be enforced
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(26) makes it an unfair trade practice to violate any rule or regulation adopted and promulgated by the Commission in the public interest and consistent with the License Act — Commission rules carry the same enforceable weight as the enumerated statutory acts.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A subdivider who has already received an original certificate under the License Act later fails to comply with ongoing requirements of the Act applicable to subdividers. This continuing noncompliance is:
choice_a: Only a civil contract issue between the subdivider and buyers
choice_b: Irrelevant once the original certificate has been issued
choice_c: An unfair trade practice under the License Act
choice_d: Enforceable only by local zoning boards, not the Commission
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(27) makes it an unfair trade practice for a subdivider, after the original certificate has been issued, to fail to comply with all the requirements of the Nebraska Real Estate License Act — the obligations do not end once the certificate is initially granted.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Before the Commission may censure a licensee, impose a civil fine, revoke or suspend a license, or issue a cease and desist order, the Act generally requires that the licensee:
choice_a: Be automatically disciplined with no notice, since real estate is a privileged occupation
choice_b: Be notified only through a public newspaper announcement
choice_c: First be convicted in a Nebraska district court
choice_d: Receive a copy of the complaint by an approved mail or tracking method and, unless the right is waived through a consent order, be given a hearing
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.25(1) requires the Commission to send the licensee or violator a copy of the complaint by registered mail, certified mail, tracked first-class mail, or a designated delivery service, and, unless the licensee waives the hearing right through an executed consent order, provide a hearing on the charges.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: How much advance notice of the date and place of a disciplinary hearing must the Commission generally give a licensee or violator under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.25?
choice_a: At least twenty days prior to the hearing date
choice_b: At least forty-eight hours prior to the hearing date
choice_c: At least one full year prior to the hearing date
choice_d: No advance notice is required as long as a hearing eventually occurs
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.25(2) requires the Commission to notify the licensee or violator in writing of the hearing's date and place at least twenty days prior to the date set for the hearing.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: If the licensee facing discipline is an associate broker or salesperson, §81-885.25 additionally requires the Commission to:
choice_a: Notify only the licensee, with no obligation regarding the employing broker
choice_b: Also notify the broker employing the licensee by mailing a copy of the hearing notice to the broker's last-known business address
choice_c: Automatically suspend the employing broker's license as well
choice_d: Require the employing broker to personally attend the hearing
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.25(2) provides that if the licensee is an associate broker or salesperson, the Commission must also notify the employing broker by mailing a copy of the hearing notice to the broker's last-known business address, keeping the supervising broker informed of proceedings against a licensee under their employ.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: After a disciplinary hearing, if the Commission finds a licensee guilty of violating the License Act or Commission rules, what penalty options are available under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.29?
choice_a: Referral to criminal prosecution only, with no administrative penalty
choice_b: Only a civil fine, since Nebraska law does not allow license suspension
choice_c: Revoke or suspend the license, enter an order of censure, impose a civil fine, or place the licensee on probation with a stayed suspension
choice_d: Only revocation, with no lesser penalties available
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.29 authorizes the Commission to revoke or suspend a license, enter a censure order, or impose a civil fine, and permits staying a suspension with the licensee placed on probation, after which the license is fully reinstated if probation is completed satisfactorily.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee's license suspension is stayed by the Commission, and the licensee is placed on probation instead. If the licensee violates the License Act or Commission rules again during the probationary period, what happens under §81-885.29?
choice_a: The matter must go through a brand-new complaint and hearing process before any suspension can occur
choice_b: The licensee receives an additional warning with no consequence
choice_c: The probationary period is simply extended with no further action
choice_d: The stayed suspension penalty is immediately executed
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.29 provides that any violation of the Act or Commission rules by the licensee during the probationary period causes the immediate execution of the previously stayed suspension penalty, without requiring a new proceeding to trigger that specific suspension.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.29, after a disciplinary hearing, the Commission's written findings, determination, and order must be:
choice_a: Officially signed by the chairperson and attested to by the director
choice_b: Approved by the Nebraska Attorney General before issuance
choice_c: Kept confidential from the licensee involved
choice_d: Filed only in the licensee's personal records, never made part of an official Commission record
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.29 requires that after the hearing, the Commission state its findings, determination, and order in writing, officially signed by the chairperson and attested to by the director.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A person who is not a licensee violates a specific provision of the License Act (a 'violator' rather than a licensee). Under the disciplinary framework, this individual:
choice_a: Can only be addressed through a private lawsuit, never Commission action
choice_b: Can still be subject to Commission proceedings and civil fines, since §81-885.25 and §81-885.29 apply to 'the licensee or violator'
choice_c: May be fined only by a Nebraska district court, never the Commission
choice_d: Is entirely outside the Commission's jurisdiction because they hold no license to revoke
explanation: Sections 81-885.25 and 81-885.29 both extend procedural notice rights and potential civil fines to a 'violator' (for example, someone practicing without a license) as well as to a licensee, recognizing that unlicensed practice under §81-885.03 is independently enforceable by the Commission.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under Nebraska's licensing framework, which individual holds full authority to conduct the brokerage's real estate business and to supervise its associate brokers and salespersons?
choice_a: The Nebraska Real Estate Commission's regional director
choice_b: Any salesperson with more than five years of experience
choice_c: The designated broker
choice_d: The most recently hired associate broker
explanation: Under the definitions in Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01, the 'designated broker' is the individual holding a broker's license with full authority to conduct the brokerage's real estate business activities and to supervise its associate brokers and salespersons.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under the License Act's definitions, an 'associate broker' is best described as:
choice_a: A broker who owns the brokerage but does not personally sell real estate
choice_b: An unlicensed office administrator who assists a broker with paperwork
choice_c: A salesperson who has completed at least one year of post-licensing education
choice_d: A person holding a broker's license who is nonetheless employed by another broker to participate in that broker's real estate brokerage activities
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01 defines 'associate broker' as a person licensed as a broker who is nevertheless employed by another broker to engage in the activities of a broker under that employing broker's supervision, distinguishing the associate broker from both the designated broker and an ordinary salesperson.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under the License Act's definitions, a 'salesperson' is:
choice_a: A person, other than an associate broker, who is employed by a broker to engage in real estate brokerage activities
choice_b: A person authorized to independently supervise other licensees without a broker's oversight
choice_c: An unlicensed assistant who helps procure potential clients
choice_d: Any person who has passed the broker's examination but not yet paid the license fee
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01 defines 'salesperson' as a person (other than an associate broker) employed by a broker to engage in the activities of a broker or salesperson, always operating under the employing broker's licensed authority rather than independently.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under the License Act's definitions, a 'team' consists of:
choice_a: A brokerage's entire administrative staff, licensed or not
choice_b: Two or more licensed persons who work under the same broker's supervision, collaborate on transactions, and hold themselves out to the public as a unified group
choice_c: Two or more separately licensed brokerages who cooperate on a single transaction
choice_d: Any group of three or more brokers who share office space regardless of supervision structure
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01 defines 'team' as two or more licensed persons operating under the same broker's supervision who work together on transactions and present themselves publicly as a unified team — teams remain fully subordinate to a single designated broker's supervision.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under the License Act's definitions, a 'team leader' is:
choice_a: Automatically the designated broker of the brokerage
choice_b: Any unlicensed office manager who coordinates team schedules
choice_c: A licensed person appointed by the broker to lead a team
choice_d: A title used interchangeably with 'associate broker' under the statute
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01 defines 'team leader' as a licensed person appointed by the broker to lead a team — a distinct role from the designated broker, though the team leader still operates under the designated broker's ultimate supervisory authority.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker opens a second office location in a different city while continuing to operate the original office. Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.19, what must the broker obtain for the additional location?
choice_a: Approval from the Nebraska Secretary of State only
choice_b: Nothing additional, since one broker's license covers unlimited locations
choice_c: A separate full broker's license held by a different individual for each branch
choice_d: A branch office license for each additional place of business maintained within the state
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.19(2) requires a broker who maintains more than one place of business within the state to obtain a branch office license for each additional branch office, subject to an annual fee capped by the Commission.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.19, who must serve as the manager of a licensed branch office?
choice_a: The broker or an associate broker
choice_b: An unlicensed office administrator designated by the broker
choice_c: Any licensed salesperson, regardless of experience level
choice_d: The Nebraska Real Estate Commission's assigned regional inspector
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.19(2) specifies that the broker or an associate broker shall be the manager of a branch office — ordinary salespersons and unlicensed staff cannot serve in this supervisory role.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee wants to also represent a different real estate broker's client on the side, in addition to working for her employing broker, without telling her employing broker. This is prohibited under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(7), which bars:
choice_a: Ever working for more than one broker over the course of a career
choice_b: Representing or attempting to represent a real estate broker other than the employer, without the employer's express knowledge and consent
choice_c: Attending continuing education courses offered by competing brokerages
choice_d: Referring clients to any other licensee under any circumstances
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(7) prohibits a licensee from representing or attempting to represent a real estate broker other than the employer without the employer's express knowledge and consent — the employing broker must be aware of and agree to any outside representation.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: An associate broker accepts a side payment from a mortgage lender for referring buyers, without ever informing her employing broker of this arrangement. This is prohibited under §81-885.24(8), which bars:
choice_a: Lenders from ever paying real estate licensees for referrals under any circumstances
choice_b: Any licensee from ever accepting a referral fee, even with full disclosure
choice_c: An associate broker or salesperson accepting any form of compensation from anyone other than his or her employing broker without the employing broker's consent
choice_d: Only designated brokers, not associate brokers, from accepting outside payments
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(8) prohibits an associate broker or salesperson from accepting compensation or consideration from anyone other than the employing broker without that broker's consent — the point is transparency and control by the employing broker, not an absolute ban on all outside compensation with proper consent.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A salesperson receives a buyer's earnest money check at a Sunday open house. Consistent with §81-885.24(24), the salesperson's obligation is to:
choice_a: Wait until closing to give the funds to the broker
choice_b: Mail the funds directly to the title company without informing the broker
choice_c: Keep the funds until Monday and deposit them personally into the salesperson's own bank account
choice_d: Deliver the funds into the custody of the employing broker as soon after receipt as practicable, so the broker can fulfill the trust account deposit deadline
explanation: Because only the broker (not an individual salesperson or associate broker) maintains the required trust account under §81-885.24(5), §81-885.24(24) requires the salesperson to place funds received in the broker's custody as soon after receipt as practicable, which also supports the broker's ability to meet the 72-hour deposit rule.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A designated broker delegates day-to-day file review to an office manager but never personally reviews whether salespersons are complying with the License Act's listing, purchase agreement, and closing statement delivery requirements. If violations of §81-885.24(19)-(21) occur repeatedly across the office, the designated broker's lack of oversight is relevant because:
choice_a: The designated broker holds full authority over, and supervisory responsibility for, the brokerage's real estate activities, including its associate brokers and salespersons
choice_b: Only the Commission, not the designated broker, bears any responsibility for salesperson conduct
choice_c: Supervisory duties apply only to associate brokers, never to salespersons
choice_d: Designated brokers have no supervisory duties once salespersons are licensed
explanation: Under the definition of 'designated broker' in Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01, that individual holds full authority to conduct the brokerage's business and to supervise its associate brokers and salespersons — a role that carries responsibility for ensuring the office's compliance with statutory requirements like recordkeeping and disclosure obligations.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A brokerage forms a new team, and the team leader begins advertising under a distinct team name while all team members remain licensed under the same designated broker. Which combination of statutory duties applies to this arrangement?
choice_a: The team is treated as its own separately licensed brokerage entity
choice_b: The team leader must keep the designated broker informed of team membership, the designated broker must record all team leaders and members, and any team advertising must not suggest independence from the brokerage
choice_c: None of the standard License Act provisions apply once a team is formed, since teams are a purely informal marketing convenience
choice_d: Only the advertising rules apply; recordkeeping duties are waived for teams
explanation: Formation of a team triggers multiple linked duties under the License Act: the team leader's duty to provide a current membership list to the designated broker (§81-885.24(31)), the designated broker's duty to maintain records of team leaders and members (§81-885.24(32)), and the prohibition on team advertising suggesting independence from the brokerage (§81-885.24(34)).

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: An associate broker is employed by Broker A but occasionally helps close deals informally for Broker B, a personal friend, without telling Broker A. If Broker B pays the associate broker directly for this help, how many separate provisions of §81-885.24 have most likely been violated?
choice_a: None, because associate brokers may freely work for multiple brokers simultaneously
choice_b: Only one, because the two provisions address identical conduct and cannot both apply
choice_c: At least two — representing another broker without the employer's consent, and accepting compensation from someone other than the employing broker without consent
choice_d: Zero, because only salespersons, not associate brokers, are bound by these provisions
explanation: This scenario implicates both §81-885.24(7) (representing a broker other than the employer without the employer's express knowledge and consent) and §81-885.24(8) (accepting compensation from someone other than the employing broker without consent) — two distinct but related unfair trade practices, both of which apply to associate brokers as well as salespersons.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A team leader is also functioning informally as if she were the designated broker, making unilateral decisions about office policy without the actual designated broker's involvement. Under the License Act's structure, this arrangement is problematic because:
choice_a: Team leaders have more authority than designated brokers under the statute
choice_b: Team leaders and designated brokers are legally interchangeable titles under Nebraska law
choice_c: Only the Commission may appoint a team leader, not the broker
choice_d: A team leader is a role appointed by the broker to lead a team, distinct from and subordinate to the designated broker, who alone holds full authority to conduct the brokerage's business and supervise all licensees
explanation: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.01, a 'team leader' is a licensed person appointed by the broker to lead a team, while the 'designated broker' is the individual with full authority to conduct the brokerage's business and supervise associate brokers and salespersons — the team leader role does not supplant or equal the designated broker's supervisory authority.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A brokerage promotes a 'cash offer now, list with us later' program in which sellers who accept a quick cash offer must agree the brokerage will handle the eventual resale listing. Reviewing this program for License Act compliance, which two provisions are most directly implicated?
choice_a: The prohibition on right-to-list home sale agreements, and the general advertising accuracy requirement if the program's terms are marketed in a misleading way
choice_b: The team advertising rule and the disputed funds rule
choice_c: The subdivider compliance requirement and the definitions statute
choice_d: The branch office licensing statute and the felony-conviction provision
explanation: A program requiring sellers to commit the brokerage to the future resale listing squarely implicates the §81-885.24(37) prohibition on right-to-list home sale agreements, and if the program's benefits or terms are advertised inaccurately, the §81-885.24(2) advertising-accuracy requirement is also implicated.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker's trust account is examined by the Commission and found to be short by several thousand dollars due to a bookkeeping error rather than intentional misappropriation. Under the License Act's disciplinary framework, is an honest bookkeeping error a defense to a trust account violation?
choice_a: No, because trust account rules apply only to intentional theft, never bookkeeping errors
choice_b: Not necessarily — §81-885.24(3)-(5) impose an objective duty to properly account for, remit, and separately deposit client funds, and a shortage can constitute a violation regardless of the broker's intent, though intent may affect the severity of any penalty imposed
choice_c: Yes, any shortage caused by an honest mistake can never be the basis for discipline
choice_d: Yes, but only if the broker self-reports within 24 hours
explanation: The trust account duties in §81-885.24(3)-(5) are framed in terms of failing to account for, remit, or properly deposit funds — an objective standard. While the Commission may consider intent (or lack thereof) in deciding on the severity of discipline under §81-885.29, an honest bookkeeping error does not automatically excuse the underlying shortage.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A brokerage's advertising for a new listing states, 'Won't last long — five offers already!' when in fact no offers have been received. This claim is best analyzed under:
choice_a: The trust account commingling prohibition
choice_b: The branch office manager requirement
choice_c: The prohibition on intentionally using advertising that is misleading or inaccurate in a material particular
choice_d: The team leader recordkeeping requirement
explanation: A false claim about existing competing offers is designed to create urgency based on a materially inaccurate statement, which falls within the §81-885.24(2) prohibition on advertising that is intentionally misleading or inaccurate in a material particular.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker keeps a well-organized set of individual client ledgers for the trust account but has not reconciled the trust account against the bank statement in over a year. Under Title 299, Chapter 3 general trust account principles, this failure to reconcile is significant because:
choice_a: Reconciliation is optional as long as ledgers exist
choice_b: Reconciliation is required only once, at the time the account is first opened
choice_c: Only the bank, not the broker, is responsible for reconciling the trust account
choice_d: Regular reconciliation is what allows a broker to detect shortages, errors, or commingling before they become larger compliance failures
explanation: The purpose of the general trust account maintenance requirements in Title 299, Chapter 3 is to ensure that a broker's records accurately reflect the true state of client funds; regular reconciliation against bank statements is the primary control that catches shortages or errors (including innocent bookkeeping mistakes) before they compound.
source_note: NREC Rules and Regulations, Title 299, Chapter 3

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker manages a rental property and holds a $1,500 security deposit. The tenant moves out, and the broker attempts to mail a refund check to the tenant's last known address, but it is returned as undeliverable and further attempts to locate the tenant fail. What must eventually happen to these unclaimed funds under Nebraska law?
choice_a: They must be turned over to the State Treasurer's Unclaimed Property Division 60 days after becoming unclaimed, under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act
choice_b: The funds remain in the trust account indefinitely with no further action required
choice_c: The funds must be donated to a local housing nonprofit chosen by the broker
choice_d: The broker may keep the funds as additional compensation for the inconvenience
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1416 requires that unclaimed residential security deposits be remitted to the State Treasurer's Unclaimed Property Division after 60 days, rather than being retained by the broker or landlord or disposed of at their discretion.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: An investigation reveals that a broker has been depositing client trust funds into her personal money market account that also holds her retirement savings, believing this was fine because she tracked each client's contribution in a personal spreadsheet. Which two unfair trade practices has she most clearly committed?
choice_a: Discriminating in the showing of property and violating fair housing statutes
choice_b: Commingling money or property of principals with her own, and failing to maintain and deposit funds in a separate trust account
choice_c: Guaranteeing future profits and violating the branch office statute
choice_d: Blockbusting and filing a cloud on title
explanation: Using a personal account for client funds — even with good personal recordkeeping — violates both §81-885.24(4) (commingling money or property of principals with the licensee's own) and §81-885.24(5) (failing to maintain and deposit all money received in a separate trust account), since a personal spreadsheet does not substitute for a properly separated trust account.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker's advertising campaign is technically accurate about every property feature but omits the fact that a home is located in a designated flood zone, a fact the broker knows but does not consider part of standard advertising content. Whether this omission constitutes a violation of §81-885.24(2) most depends on:
choice_a: Whether the ad was published online versus in print
choice_b: Nothing — omissions can never violate the advertising provision, only affirmative false statements can
choice_c: Whether the omission renders the advertising misleading or inaccurate in a material particular, considering what a reasonable buyer would find significant
choice_d: Whether the broker used the word 'flood' anywhere else in prior marketing
explanation: Section 81-885.24(2)'s standard turns on whether advertising is misleading or inaccurate in a material particular; a material omission that leaves a false overall impression (such as omitting a known flood zone designation while touting other features) can be analyzed under the same materiality standard as an affirmative misstatement.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A team's promotional material states, 'The Anderson Group — Your Independent Local Experts,' without mentioning that all team members are licensed under XYZ Realty, the designated brokerage. This phrasing is problematic chiefly because of the word:
choice_a: 'Experts,' since no licensee may ever claim expertise in advertising
choice_b: 'Local,' since only statewide brokerages may use geographic descriptors
choice_c: 'Group,' since teams may never use the word 'group' in their name
choice_d: 'Independent,' since it suggests the team operates as its own brokerage separate from XYZ Realty
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.24(34) specifically targets team advertising or team names suggesting the team is an independent real estate brokerage; the word 'Independent' in this slogan directly implies a status the team, as a group operating under a single designated broker, does not actually have.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A broker's listing agreements are all pre-printed with a permanent, undated expiration clause that reads 'this agreement continues until terminated by either party,' with no specific end date entered on any of them. Across the broker's entire book of listings, this template most likely creates a pattern of violating:
choice_a: The requirement to include a fixed date of expiration in every written listing agreement
choice_b: The requirement to maintain a trust account
choice_c: The requirement to notify the employing broker of outside compensation
